Definition: apparently a primary word; "halt", i.e. limping:--cripple, halt, lame.
BiblicalUsage: Cholos is lame, one who halts and cannot walk, and the Gospels use it for the people Jesus heals. The lame walk when John asks whether Jesus is the one to come, the lame man at the Beautiful gate is healed and leaps up, and the blind and the halt lie waiting at the pool of Bethesda.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lame in these stories are the picture of every sinner, unable to walk until Christ bids them rise. I hold that the healing of the lame is the proof of the kingdom, because it is what the prophets promised.
RelatedEvents: Peter Heals the Lame Man; The Healing at the Pool of Bethesda
